subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls (PII, RBAC, break-glass)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@fintrust.com>, Ryana Smith <ryana.smith@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls (PII, RBAC, break-glass)

Hi Daniel & Ryana,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand FinTrust's use case and risk surface. Quick recap and a few questions so we can scope next steps for a secure Dedicated/Private deployment that meets your compliance needs.

Key takeaways from today's discussion:
- Workload: customer support automation + account summarization (sensitive PII will be passed to model inference).
- Data residency: US-only (must be hosted in us-east region, no cross-region backups).
- PII types: full name, DOB, SSN, routing/account numbers.
- Retention: you requested retention policies for raw inputs and logs (discussed 30 days vs longer retention for audit).
- Support access: FinTrust requires break-glass procedures with documented approvals, time-limited access, and full audit logs.
- RBAC: least-privilege roles for platform, SSO integration (Okta), and per-team isolation via dedicated projects.

Open questions for you (so we can confirm the design/estimate):
1) Final retention window for logs and raw inputs for compliance/audit (you mentioned 7 years for some records — can you confirm which record types require that)?
2) Any additional encryption requirements beyond CMK (HSM) + customer-managed KMS?
3) Is FinTrust comfortable with Redwood providing a Private deployment in your VPC or would you prefer Redwood-hosted Dedicated in an isolated tenant?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share the security questionnaire (or we can complete the attached SOC2 summary + access controls matrix), we’ll turn this into a proposed design and SOW.
- Internal touchpoint with our security lead (Rishi) and solutions architect (Neha) — can meet early next week.

I’ve attached a 1-pager SOC2 summary and our access controls matrix template to help speed this along.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, access_controls_matrix.xlsx

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryana Smith <ryana.smith@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls (PII, RBAC, break-glass)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the docs. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Retention: For transaction-level financial records (account/routing numbers) we are required to retain certain records for up to 7 years for audit purposes. For conversational logs (support chats), 90 days retention is preferred unless escalated for investigation.
- Data residency: Confirmed — all production data and backups must remain in us-east-1. No replicated backups to other regions.
- PII: Yes, SSNs and full account numbers are in scope. We need tokenization/pseudonymization options for long-term storage.
- Support access / break-glass: We require just-in-time privileged access (JIT), multi-party approval for break-glass, session recording, and immutable audit logs stored for 7 years. Access must be requested via our ticketing system and tied to an incident ID.
- RBAC: We use Okta with SCIM provisioning and need role mappings for engineering, SRE, and support. Least privilege for production model endpoints is non-negotiable.

I’ve attached the FinTrust security questionnaire (partially redacted) — it covers encryption, logging, and vendor access policies. Please share a proposed architecture that maps to these controls.

Also would like to schedule a call with Rishi & Neha next Tue 10am ET if they’re available.

Thanks,
Daniel Kim
Head of Security, FinTrust
daniel.kim@fintrust.com

Attachments: fintrust_security_questionnaire.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@fintrust.com>, Ryana Smith <ryana.smith@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls (PII, RBAC, break-glass)

Great, thanks for the detail Daniel — that helps a lot. Rishi/Neha: looping you both in to propose an initial alignment and to own the technical design / runbook.

Initial proposal (high level):
- Deployment: Private deployment option in FinTrust VPC (preferred) with customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed). Alternatively, Dedicated isolated tenant in us-east with tenant-level isolation and no cross-region backups.
- Data handling: optional tokenization service before long-term persistence; ephemeral raw input retention configurable per workspace (default 30 days), logs retention configurable up to 7 years for audit.
- RBAC & SSO: SCIM + Okta provisioning, role templates for SRE/engineers/support, attribute-based access controls for model endpoints (read vs invoke vs admin).
- Break-glass & Support Access: Just-in-time privileged access integrated with FinTrust ticketing (we can accept incident ID as approval), multi-party approval flow, session recording, and immutable audit events sent to your SIEM (or stored in customer-controlled S3 with versioning). All access events are exportable for audits.

Action items / next steps:
1) Rishi/Neha to produce a 1-2 page architecture diagram + runbook (including break-glass flow) and a filled access_controls_matrix by EOD Tue.
2) Marissa to deliver SOW + estimate once architecture is agreed.
3) Schedule technical deep-dive with Rishi & Neha — Daniel proposed Tue 10am ET, can you confirm?

Daniel — once you confirm the retention mapping (which object types require 7yrs vs 90/30 days), we’ll finalize the matrix and SOW.

Thanks all,
Marissa

Attachments: access_controls_matrix.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls (PII, RBAC, break-glass)

Thumbs up on the approach. I’ll own the runbook and break-glass playbook; Neha will draft the architecture diagram and the filled access_controls_matrix. We’ll include:
- JIT with MFA + OAuth token tied to ticket/incident ID
- Multi-party approval (min 2) for break-glass
- Time-limited access (max 4 hours by default) with automatic revocation
- Full session recording + immutable audit logs (exportable to FinTrust SIEM)
- SCIM mappings for Okta + least-privilege default roles

We’ll aim to have the artifacts and a draft SOW by EOD Tue so Marissa can put together pricing.

-Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
